description: Hi! I'm Muhammedzhan from Shymkent. I have been building robots since 2018.
summary:
We developed alansyz, a 25 minute mission game inside Roblox. The player flies to the Moon, lands on Mars, keeps a small base alive for ten sols and refuels a rocket to get home.

The game answers the challenge with one simple rule. The base has one battery and it is never enough. Air and heat, food, radiation shelter, the radio and the oxygen plant for the rocket all pull from the same energy, so no choice is free and every decision teaches a real mission trade off.

The danger comes from real NASA data. At launch the game checks NASA DONKI for solar flares from the last three days, and a real flare becomes the storm the player must survive. Frost nights come from Curiosity REMS, oxygen production follows MOXIE on Perseverance, and the radio delay follows today's true distance to Mars. Sources are shown in the game, and archive data is labeled as archive.

This matters because young people usually meet space as something they only watch. alansyz lets them run a mission themselves, anywhere, on the phone, tablet or computer they already use.
details:
What it does

alansyz is a mission game inside Roblox that takes about 25 minutes. A short prologue on Earth sets the story. A cabin flight shows launch, g force and weightlessness. On the Moon the player carries ice from a permanently shadowed crater to an electrolyzer and turns it into fuel. After a landing scene on Mars, ten sols begin. The player builds an oxygen plant, a greenhouse, solar panels, a battery and an antenna, drills rocks for rare samples, and shelters from frost nights, dust storms and solar storms. The mission ends when ten oxygen tanks are loaded and the rocket leaves in its launch window.

How it works

The game is built in Roblox Studio with Luau. One server side economy controls energy, air, food, radiation and fuel. When a mission starts, the game asks NASA DONKI for solar flares from the last three days. If there is a real flare, that flare with its class and date hits the base. If there is none, the game draws one of 37 X class flares from our DONKI archive and says so on screen. Night temperatures come from 120 nights measured by the REMS station on Curiosity in Gale crater. The distance between Earth and Mars and the radio delay are computed for today from JPL orbital elements, and one real minute of signal delay becomes one second of waiting. The screen shows one goal at a time with a glowing path to it, so a young player always knows what to do next.

Benefits

Players learn by doing, not by reading. They feel why oxygen, energy and shelter matter on another planet because they run out of them. Facts from MOXIE, Phoenix, Veggie, LCROSS and the Apollo soil experiments appear at the moment they matter, never as a wall of text. The game runs on the phones, tablets and computers young people already own.

Intended impact

We want every player to walk away understanding one true rule of deep space survival. There is never enough power for everything, and every choice has a cost. Next we will open the game to players of every age, add a short quiz before and after the mission to measure what players learn, add Kazakh and English, and grow it into a crew mission where each friend plays a role on the base.

Tools

Roblox Studio and Luau for the game, Python and Node.js for downloading and preparing NASA data, and ffmpeg for the demo video. We balanced the mission with 26 automated checks that run the same economy as the game.

What makes it creative

The storm a player survives may be a flare that really left the Sun this week, and the radio delay changes every day with the real orbits of Earth and Mars. We also chose not to build our own engine. In two days it would have given players a flat and dry experience. Roblox has developed its engine for 20 years, invested 1.57 billion dollars in research and development in 2025 alone, and about 138 million people play on it every day. So all our time went into the mission and the science.

What we considered

No safe choice. When a flare comes, hiding costs radiation, covering the base with soil costs energy, and staying outside to mine ice costs much more radiation. Honest data. Every source is named on screen, and archive data is never shown as live. Balance. A careful crew makes it home, while a crew that sends all its energy to the rocket freezes on sol five or six. Plain language. One goal at a time and short facts instead of long text.

How to play

The game page opens without an account. To play, a free Roblox account is needed, as for any Roblox game. Right now players aged 16 and older can join, and younger players will join after the standard review that Roblox runs for every new game.

We began prototyping on November 8 with written permission from our Local Lead, and our git history shows the real dates.
